ops.title: daemonkit v1 remediation: the six root causes and the 4-release collapse
ops.body:
Approved 2026-07-27. Supersedes ad-hoc stabilization. Session plan file: `~/.claude/plans/codex-has-been-churning-robust-aurora.md`.

## Why

A runaway 150-agent codex swarm (Jul 17-24 2026, depth-6, ~1.8B tokens) authored **97.6% of this repo in a 3-day window**. What survives is not a design; it is sediment. At the start of remediation: 16 root packages, ~30k source lines, **747 exported symbols of which ~366 (49%) have zero callers anywhere in the fleet**, 25 tags in 4 days, 127/150 commits with no body, 37 band-aid vs 19 root-cause commits, and README/AGENTS/doc.go still advertising `drain/` and `supervise/` — deleted in `2b912d6` (−21,224 lines, no body, no decision record).

The user's mandate, verbatim: *"a lot of this seems to be stemming from a ton of overcomplication/over-engineering bandaids; lets get back to basics, use what we've learned to implement this clean, once, with the right abstractions, patterns, and healing, and get rid of all the cruft and bandaids"* — with the execution bar *"but very well tested and specced, lets not make the mistakes again, make sure we maintain feature parity from anything downstream actually needs, and read the entire commit history to bake in all the lessons (and all the ccn, but figure out what is correct vs obsolete)."*

## The six root causes

Every open backlog item and every band-aid rolls up under one of these.

- **RC1 — Ownership by ceremony, not by one authority.** daemonkit never committed to one answer to *"who owns this process and is it alive?"*, so ~20 proof mechanisms accreted: a reap-receipt ledger with sequences/floors/digests, recovery capabilities, stop authorities, fence/runtime/spawnedsession capability tokens, worker claims, three stacked lifecycle machines, a `/bin/sh` spawn gate with `trap ':' TERM`. The one real safety property — the 4-field kill authority — got buried. The ledger gates nothing: its sole fleet consumer verifies then unconditionally acks (`cc-orchestrate/ptyhost/host.go:226-232`), and `service/` acks its own receipts with literal no-op callbacks (`service/controller.go:204-218`).
- **RC2 — Durable state as replayable intent, validated at load.** Stores persist environment-derived facts and replay them with launchctl side effects at open: `NewController` runs `reconcile()` at `service/controller.go:203` and fails the open on error. Every schema is fail-closed exact-fingerprint with no forward path, so state written by a broken era blocks the fixed release that would supersede it.
- **RC3 — Exact-match-everything, migrated by flag-day hard cut.** Build strings (`wire/server.go:614`), seven redundant version axes, and schema fingerprints all assert exact equality with no migration story. Normal pin skew across 10 independently-released consumers is redefined as hard failure, and the mixed-era boundary has no test — 18,999 handshake failures over 5 days with green CI everywhere.
- **RC4 — No outcome taxonomy at OS boundaries.** launchctl exit codes, OSStatus and errno consumed as raw ints at N call sites with two *disagreeing* classifiers (`service/controller.go:641` vs `keepalive.go:529`). `launchctlInFluxExit = 5` classifies a permanent EPERM as transient, retries 6x, and misreports it as a session-type problem — a diagnostic that sent one investigation down nine dead ends and shipped v0.20.8, which fixed nothing and regressed the machine.
- **RC5 — Machinery exported as API; the assembly never shipped.** *"The packages ARE the deliberate public API"* turned every internal mechanism into a 747-symbol compatibility obligation, while the one assembly every consumer needs — serve a daemon, wait until ready, upgrade — never shipped. Six repos hand-roll the same 7-step activation ladder. Peer trust runs as a fork/exec of `os.Executable()`, putting a fork-bomb primitive and a load-dependent startup probe into every consumer.
- **RC6 — Unreviewed swarm authorship and a release process that shipped guesses.** The most-reviewed subsystem in the repo was deleted in one bodyless commit. 4 of the last 9 releases were code-free re-cuts. Nobody can distinguish load-bearing invariants from agent guesses, so every remediation session starts with archaeology.

## The three primitives v1 is built from

- **Ownership/liveness — one authority.** `proc.Record{PID, StartTime, Boot, Comm, Session, Owner, Label}`, all four identity fields revalidated against the live process table immediately before any signal. `Liveness` is tri-state and **Undetermined is never Dead**. `proc.FileLock` (inode identity, never unlinked, polling) for singletons. `OwnerGeneration` names the incarnation. ONE lifecycle enum, owned by `daemon`: `starting → ready → draining → closed`. Recovery = flock → load → revalidate → TERM → grace → revalidate → KILL → remove. *The durable record is the proof* — ledger, sequences, floors and claims all delete as derived state.
- **Healing — observe and converge, with typed drift.** Reconcile **observes, never replays**; desired state is the caller's fresh set every call; current state is read from the world (plist bytes, `launchctl print`, the process table). Load decodes structurally and never validates the world; validation runs at write/effect time. Wrong-schema state **archives aside with a logged path — never a fatal open**. Teardown of a running agent happens only after its replacement proved loadable. Anything destructive is opt-in consumer config.
- **Upgrade — one compatibility axis per surface.** Wire: exact `ProtocolVersion`, build as diagnostic only. Durable state: a schema int + the uniform archive-aside rule (the 5 fingerprint constants delete). Binaries: digest-keyed `Stage` — plists only ever point at staged paths, making persisted Caskroom paths *unrepresentable*. Signed apps: attest → quiesce → atomic rename-swap → converge → verify, where the rename is the one non-idempotent step and holds the one durable receipt.

## The four releases

- **Phase 0 (no release)** — full-history lesson mining; cc-notes KEEP/HISTORICAL/WRONG triage; the **invariant census** producing four written contracts (launchctl outcomes with provenance · durable child-record lifetime · wire session lifecycle for Go *and* Swift · the converge/drift model); a feature-parity census across the 10 consumers that becomes the acceptance checklist; CI machinery (fleet-build via a generated `go.work` overlay, mixed-era test, export census); doc tombstone fixes. **Nothing is deleted until it is written down** — this phase is the anti-`2b912d6` gate.
- **Phase 1 v0.21.0 — stop the bleeding** (behavior only, zero API change): spawn gate → Go on both sides of the fork (delete `trap ':' TERM`); ONE `launchctlOutcome` classifier per OS boundary, retrying only `InFlux`; in-process trust verification (deletes the verifier child and the load-dependent startup probe); strong settlement restored (`Done()` ⇒ record gone); protocol-only handshake gate with `WireBuild` demoted to a Health diagnostic.
- **Phase 2 v0.22.0 — the operations** (additive + invisible deletions): ship `daemon.Serve`, `wire.WaitReady`, stateless `Converge → Drift`, `service.Stage`, `deployment.Upgrade/Remove/Reset`, `proc.Run`, plus the shape seams the parity census names. Delete zero-caller machinery. Record store → `ExactStateFile[[]proc.Record]` with a **one-release** bbolt read-shim. Consumer repin #1: 10 small PRs, **no lockstep**.
- **Phase 3 v0.23.0 — the collapse**: delete the orphaned machinery, ONE `ProtocolVersion` bump, Swift in the same commits, unexport to ~150 symbols, repin sweep #2 (the only lockstep event).
- **Phase 4 v1.0.0 — freeze** after v0.23 soaks: final export census, the cross-language protocol assertion, `go.mod retract [v0.1.0, v0.4.1]`, tag.

Target: **16 packages → 9 · ~30k src → ~13k · 747 exported → ~150**, CI-enforced.

## Decisions taken (do not re-litigate)

Clean-slate core, spec- and test-first · coordinated breaking v1 + fleet repin · daemonkit **keeps its scope** (`artifact/`, `ghrelease/`, `bundle/` stay — they shrink by unexporting, they do not move out) · **protocol-only** handshake gate, build as diagnostic · single-consumer packages stay in daemonkit with a shrunken API · drain is a small state on `daemon.Runtime`, not a package · v1.0.0 tagged only after the collapse soaks.

## Standing rules after v1

One release per coherent changeset · no protocol or schema bump without a consumer that needs it, a migration-or-archive path, and an upgrade note · **fleet-build or mixed-era red = no release, ever** · a band-aid landed during remediation is a failed phase.

## Hard operational rules

- **NEVER run bare `go test` in daemonkit.** `proc.Spawn` execs `os.Executable()`; a test binary re-enters the spawn and fork-bombs the machine. `scripts/test.sh` and its `RLIMIT_NPROC` cap stay even after the self-exec verifier is deleted, and no Taskfile or CI route may bypass it.
- **Sentinel identity is load-bearing across module boundaries.** Consumers alias daemonkit sentinels and match with `errors.Is` from other repos. Every consolidation keeps the old exported names as alias vars — there is no compile-time signal for this.
- **Bundle identity is a hard freeze.** macOS keys TCC/notification/FDA grants to identifier + team + install path; changing any resets the user's grants. Never byte-stage an `.app`-bundled helper out of its bundle.
ops.when: Before touching daemonkit source, planning a daemonkit release, deleting any daemonkit mechanism, or repinning a fleet consumer — during the Jul 2026 → v1.0.0 remediation
